zones.name: CODE-ZONE
zones.tagline: Architect the Future with Pure Engineering & Code
zones.description: Push your coding boundaries across modern web engineering, cutting-edge Gemini AI app creation, and rigorous codebase debugging.

zones.name: FUN-ZONE
zones.tagline: Where Wit, Tactical Mindset & Reflexes Collide
zones.description: High-octane excitement spanning the frontiers of AI trends, sharp rhetorical debate, and intense competitive multiplayer gaming.

zones.name: FIN-TECH
zones.tagline: Disrupt Financial Ecosystems & Pitch the Next Unicorn
zones.description: Unleash visionary startup concepts, pitch to industry leaders, and master market valuation and quantitative financial problem-solving.

events.name: WEBATHON
events.shortDescription: Build next-generation web platforms solving real-world challenges.
events.fullDescription: Participants design, build, and deploy high-performance web applications under time pressure. Projects are judged on functionality, visual aesthetic, UX responsiveness, clean architecture, and technical innovation.
objectives: Architect a full-stack or frontend web application within the competition timeframe
Demonstrate responsive UI design and robust state management
Deploy the working application to a live staging environment
events.eligibility: Open to all undergraduate and postgraduate college students with valid student IDs.
rules: Teams must build their projects during the designated event period.
Open-source libraries and frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind, etc.) are allowed.
Plagiarism or using pre-built full applications results in immediate disqualification.
Final submission must include a live URL and code repository link.

events.name: VIBEATHON
events.shortDescription: Participants build an application powered by Google Gemini AI.
events.fullDescription: Vibeathon challenges builders to push the envelope of multimodal generative AI. Build intelligent agents, reasoning engines, creative spatial tools, or conversational workflows powered by Google Gemini.
objectives: Implement real integration with the Google Gemini API
Leverage multimodal capabilities (text, vision, audio, reasoning)
Deliver an intuitive user workflow solving a tangible domain problem
events.eligibility: College students passionate about artificial intelligence, prompt engineering, and app development.
rules: Applications must utilize the Google Gemini API for core AI functionalities.
Solutions must handle prompt edge cases and demonstrate sensible guardrails.
Demonstrations must run live during the final judging round.

customFields.label: Brief Gemini Project Concept
customFields.placeholder: Describe what your Gemini application will accomplish

events.name: BUGVERSE
events.shortDescription: Identify, debug, and fix complex errors across modern codebases.
events.fullDescription: A multi-round speed and precision debugging arena. Participants navigate obfuscated repositories, patch memory leaks, solve concurrency deadlocks, and resolve security vulnerabilities.
objectives: Quickly diagnose faulty logic and architectural bottlenecks
Refactor broken modules without breaking existing unit tests
Optimize runtime performance and algorithmic efficiency
events.eligibility: All registered students with proficiency in C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript.
rules: Participants receive sandboxed repositories with failing test suites.
Points are awarded based on speed of resolution and test pass rate.
Automated plagiarism detection is enforced.

events.name: AI QUIZ
events.shortDescription: Fast-paced quiz on the latest AI trends, architectures, and history.
events.fullDescription: Test your grasp of foundational machine learning, LLM evolution, Transformer mechanics, autonomous systems, and modern AI industry breakthroughs in a buzzer-style quiz format.
objectives: Demonstrate broad and deep knowledge of modern AI/ML trends
Compete under high-speed round-based time limits
Navigate rapid-fire trivia and technical reasoning questions
events.eligibility: Open to all students with an appetite for AI breakthroughs.
rules: Multiple rounds: Preliminary written screening followed by buzzer-based stage finals.
Electronic devices are strictly prohibited during the quiz rounds.
Quizmaster decisions are final and binding.

events.name: DEBATE COMPETITION
events.shortDescription: Present, defend, and critique arguments on contemporary tech topics.
events.fullDescription: A premier intellectual debate tournament. Teams spar over artificial intelligence ethics, technological monopolies, quantum computing frontiers, and digital privacy policies.
objectives: Articulate rigorous logical arguments on contested technology topics
Rebut opposition arguments with factual precision and poise
Engage judges with compelling rhetoric and persuasive delivery
events.eligibility: Open to all collegiate debaters and tech enthusiasts.
rules: Parliamentary or Oxford-style debate format depending on the round.
Topic assigned 30 minutes prior to match; both affirmative and negative sides must be prepared.
Strict adherence to speaker time limits.

events.name: GAMING COMPETITION
events.shortDescription: Competitive esports showdown across high-octane multiplayer titles.
events.fullDescription: Assemble your squad for the ultimate esports arena. Compete in intense bracket-style elimination matches showcasing tactical coordination, lightning reflexes, and strategic synergy.
objectives: Compete in sanctioned esports tournament brackets
Demonstrate squad communication and clutch mechanical gameplay
Climb double-elimination brackets to championship victory
events.eligibility: All college gaming squads with active player handles.
rules: Standard competitive tournament rules and fair-play anti-cheat enforcement.
Participants must bring their own peripherals if specified.
Unsportsmanlike conduct leads to instant forfeit.

events.name: STARTUP IDEA PITCHING
events.shortDescription: Pitch groundbreaking business solutions to founders and investors.
events.fullDescription: The flagship entrepreneurship event of PLANET-X 2026. Pitch your disruptive product, market strategy, unit economics, and growth roadmap to an esteemed panel of venture capitalists and startup leaders.
objectives: Synthesize an innovative startup concept solving a verified market gap
Present a crisp 5-minute pitch deck followed by a 3-minute jury Q&A
Defend market viability, competitive moat, and revenue model
events.eligibility: Student innovators, aspiring founders, and entrepreneurial teams.
rules: Pitch deck must be submitted 24 hours prior to the live pitching session.
Strict 5-minute pitch timer followed by 3-minute jury defense.
Prototypes or MVPs earn bonus evaluation credit.

events.name: FINANCIAL QUIZ & ANALYSIS
events.shortDescription: Master quantitative financial models, valuation, and capital markets.
events.fullDescription: A two-stage finance showdown combining a fast-paced capital markets quiz with an analytical case study. Evaluate balance sheets, calculate DCF valuations, and recommend actionable investment strategies.
objectives: Exhibit acumen in macroeconomics, equity markets, and corporate finance
Analyze financial statements and identify key valuation drivers
Deliver an investment thesis backed by financial modeling
events.eligibility: Students interested in finance, commerce, economics, and analytics.
rules: Round 1: Rapid-fire screening quiz on financial markets and instruments.
Round 2: Comprehensive financial case analysis with spreadsheet submission.
Standard financial calculator allowed.
